code: # load the required libraries library(cmldiffvar) library(dplyr) #>  #> Attaching package: 'dplyr' #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union  # set the seed for reproducibility set.seed(3976468)  # simulate randomized controlled trial population n_pop <- 100000 propensity_score <- 0.5 propensity_score_vec <- rep(propensity_score, n_pop) treatment_vec <- rbinom(n_pop, 1, propensity_score) outcome_treatment_vec <- rnorm(n = n_pop, mean = 3, sd = 1.2) outcome_control_vec <- rnorm(n = n_pop, mean = 1, sd = 1) outcome_vec <- treatment_vec * outcome_treatment_vec +   (1 - treatment_vec) * outcome_control_vec population_tbl <- tibble(   propensity_score = propensity_score_vec,   treatment = treatment_vec,   outcome = outcome_vec )  # randomly sample from the population sample_tbl <- slice_sample(population_tbl, n = 500)  # estimate the relative differential variance and test the homogeneous treatment # assumption rel_diff_var_est <- sample_tbl |>   unadjdiffvar(     estimand_type = "relative",     treatment_var_name = "treatment",     propensity_score_var_name = "propensity_score",     outcome_var_name = "outcome"   )  rel_diff_var_est #> # A tibble: 1 × 6 #>   estimand                       estimate    se ci_low ci_high p_value #>   <chr>                             <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1 relative differential variance     1.51 0.187   1.14    1.87 0.00676

title: Using the cmldiffvar Package
text: cmldiffvar package implements two adjusted estimators differential variance parameter: one-step estimator (Bickel et al. 1993; Pfanzagl Wefelmeyer 1985) targeted maximum likelihood estimator (TMLE) (van der Laan Rubin 2006; van der Laan Rose 2011, 2018). Note one-step estimator equivalent estimating equation (alternatively known double/debiased machine learning estimator) (van der Laan Robins 2003; Chernozhukov et al. 2017). estimators rely estimation three nuisance parameters: propensity score: g(W)=P(=1|W)g(W) = P(=1|W), outcome regression: Q‾(W,)=E[Y|W,]\bar{Q}(W, ) = E[Y|W, ], squared outcome regression: Q‾2(W,)=E[Y2|W,]\bar{Q}^2(W, ) = E[Y^2|W, ] . adjusted estimators doubly robust. , g(W)g(W) Q‾(W,)\bar{Q}(W, ) Q‾2(W,)\bar{Q}^2(W, ) consistently estimated, adjusted estimators consistent well. , nuisance estimators g(W)g(W), Q‾(W,)\bar{Q}(W, ), Q‾2(W,)\bar{Q}^2(W, ) consistent converge rate n1/4n^{1/4} L2L_2 norm, estimators regular asymptotically linearly. implies differential variance parameter estimators’ sampling distributions asymptotically normal true differential variance parameters variance given parameters’ efficient influence functions. unadjusted estimators, 95% Wald-type confidence intervals can turn constructed, hypotheses treatment effect heterogeneity can performed. Additional details provided Boileau et al. (preparation). Now, package relies Super Learners flexibly estimate g(W)g(W), Q‾(W,)\bar{Q}(W, ), Q‾2(W,)\bar{Q}^2(W, )(van der Laan, Polley, Hubbard 2007). particular, cmldiffvar package relies SuperLearner R package implementation ensemble learning framework. default, generalized linear model, multivariate adaptive regression splines (Friedman 1991), Random Forest (Breiman 2001) used base learners Super Learner estimator propensity score outcome regression. generalized quadratic linear model Random Forest make base learners Super Learner estimator squared outcome regression. course, alternative set base learners used estimator can specified cmldiffvar() function. Finally, note adjusted estimators guaranteed regular asymptotically linear applied data generated randomized controlled trial. known propensity scores, corresponding study units arm randomization probabilities, can provided cmldiffvar() function using propensity_score_var_name argument.

title: Causal Machine Learning Methods for Differential Variance Inference
text: cmldiffvar implements causal machine learning methods differential variance inference. methods rely semiparametric efficiency theory flexible machine learning methods — namely, Super Learner ensembles — avoid need convenience assumptions data-generating processes (van der Laan Rose 2011; van der Laan, Polley, Hubbard 2007). Hypothesis tests differential variance can uncover heterogeneous treatment effects, even effect modifiers excluded data. Details methodology provided Boileau et al. (preparation).

title: Causal Machine Learning Methods for Differential Variance Inference
text: estimate absolute differential variance, defined difference potential outcomes’ standard deviations, random sample toy_population_tbl data included cmldiffvar package. dataset represents observational study treatment variable binary, outcome continuous, single confounder measured. true absolute differential variance population 22. absolute differential variance non-zero, treatment effect heterogeneous. use targeted maximum likelihood estimator (van der Laan Rubin 2006; van der Laan Rose 2011, 2018), cmldiffvar() function’s default estimator, infer differential variance population. function outputs point estimate 95%95\% confidence interval default. p-value corresponding test whether differential variance significantly different zero also provided. equivalent testing whether treatment effect homogeneous. absolute differential variance point estimate near ground truth. Additionally, test correctly rejects null hypothesis homogeneous treatment effect 5%5\% significance level.
code: # load the required packages library(cmldiffvar) library(dplyr) library(SuperLearner)  # set the seed for reproducibility set.seed(510)  # random sample from population data sample_tbl <- slice_sample(toy_population_tbl, n = 250)  # estimate absolute differential variance dif_var_result_tbl <- sample_tbl |>   cmldiffvar(     propensity_score_adj_var_names = "confounder",     cond_exp_outcome_adj_var_names = "confounder",     treatment_var_name = "treatment",     outcome_var_name = "outcome"   )
